pr_body:
The naïve matching algorithm we previously used to match declarations in
source files to declarations in typings files was based only on the name
of the thing being declared.  This did not handle cases where the declared
item has been exported via an alias. This is a common scenariow when one
of the two file sets (source or typings) has been flattened, while the other
has not.

The new algorithm tries to overcome this by creating two maps of export
name to declaration (i.e. `Map<string, ts.Declaration>`).
One for the source files and one for the typings files.
It then joins these two together by matching export names, resulting in a
new map that maps source declarations to typings declarations directly
(i.e. `Map<ts.Declaration, ts.Declaration>`).

This new map can handle the declaration names being different between the
source and typings as long as they are ultimately both exported with the
same alias name.

Fixes #33593
Fixes #34191
Fixes #32442

issue_context.title: Ivy error TS-996002, when using compiled esm5 files
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/cli ### Is this a regression? It only happens when Ivy is enabled - ngcc. With stable ngc AOT build it works fine. ### Description The error occurs when running the `ng build` command, if the source code imports a module and component from a compiled esm5 file, which has the associated `d.ts` and `metadata.json` files. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Can be found here: https://github.com/acidb/mobiscroll-ivy-test Running `ng build` throws the mentioned error. ## 🔥 Exception or Error 

ERROR in src/mobiscroll/src/js/input.angular.d.ts:3:22 - error TS-996002: Appears in the NgModule.imports of AppModule, but could not be resolved to an NgModule class

3 export declare class MbscInputModule {
## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 9.0.0-next.0
Node: 12.4.0
OS: win32 x64
Angular: 9.0.0-next.3
... animations, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms
... language-service, platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic
... router

comments:
The same issue for Nebular: https://github.com/akveo/nebular/issues/1613
And not working with 8.2.11.
I am able to reproduce this with ng2-pdfjs-viewer. Repro repo here: https://github.com/biltongza/ng2-pdfjs-viewer-ivy-es2015

I figured a few things out

1 - If a compiled esm5 file is referenced from a folder in the src folder, it does not work. I guess this is because `ngcc` only compiles packages inside `node_modules` to make them ivy compatible? We distribute our library as a downloadable package - currently this will only work with ivy if it's packaged using `npm pack` and install it to `node_modules` from the generated file.

2 - `ngcc` will also fail with esm5 file containing minified code. Renaming variables definitely makes it fail. I tried to keep the name of the component classes, which resulted in successful build, but runtime failure.
Created a reproduction repo with the minified fesm5 file: https://github.com/acidb/mobiscroll-ivy-test/tree/test

Looking into this...

---

By the way, you can also point ngcc at folders other than `node_modules`:

```
-s, --source      A path (relative to the working directory) of the
                    `node_modules` folder to process.[default: "./node_modules"]
```
But it is a bit tricky since your mobiscroll folder does not contain a package.json to describe the entry-points. But it should be possible to overcome that too using an `ngcc.config.js` file.

@dioslaska - you'll be glad to hear that after https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/34254 lands your test reproduction will build without error! See https://github.com/acidb/mobiscroll-ivy-test/pull/1/files

I know that there are a number of minification scenarios that we do not support in ngcc right now.
Can I ask what is the motivation/use case for minifying your library code?
* If you are bundling the final app, then minification can be done there, so there is no size benefit in minifying the imported library
* some people think that minfication obfuscates their code. I am sure this is not the case here - especially as the original source if available on github.

@dioslaska - can you respond to my question? In general heavily minifying library code is not very useful. There are lots of potential minification scenarios that make it almost impossible for ngcc to be able to reverse engineer what is going on, so that it can process it.
Please do test with the latest RC. We did a bit of work in this area to help support another package that was doing some minifying of their code...

I did test it with rc8 and here are my findings:

1. Transpiled classes not wrapped inside extra paranthesis are still not working, so `wrap_iife` and post process replace is still needed, but now fails with a different error message: `No typings declaration can be found for the referenced NgModule class in function(e){return{ngModule:MbscModule,providers:[{provide:MbscRouterToken,useExisting:e.angularRouter}]}}.`

2. `keep_fnames` - this is not needed anymore, works fine without.

3. `reserved: ['_super']` - this is still needed to prevent renaming the `_super` parameter of an inherited class. If removed, the compilation runs fine, but will throw a runtime error.

4. `join_vars` - still does not work, but now fails with a different error message: `No typings declaration can be found for the referenced NgModule class in function(e){return{ngModule:MbscModule,providers:[{provide:MbscRouterToken,useExisting:e.angularRouter}]}}.`

5. `reduce_vars` - this works now

6. `sequences` - still does not work, the error remained the same: `could not be resolved to an NgModule class`

7. Additionally I got a new error message: `The target entry point @mobiscroll/angular has missing dependencies"
This is caused by the fact that my typescript entry file imports a plain js file (`import './mobiscroll.common`) - the import will be present in the generated `d.ts` file as well, but the referenced js file will of course not be present in the generated package. I solved this by removing the import from the `.d.ts` file, but this worked with rc4 - meaning that our versions, which worked with rc4, are no longer working with rc8. Any input on this?

So my understanding of the current state is:

* 1, 3, 4 and 6 are still unsupported by ngcc
* I believe that 7 should now be fixed after various recent PRs including https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/34695

If you could provide simple reproductions of 1, 4 and 6 I think we could get them working. I doubt we could easily support 3.

I am going to close this issue now. Let's open individual issues for the items above if we are going to try to solve them. Thanks for your excellent analysis and feedback @dioslaska .

`ERROR in Failed to compile entry-point angular-tree-component (module as esm5) due to compilation errors: node_modules/mobx-angular/dist/mobx-angular.d.ts:8:22 - error NG6002: Appears in the NgModule.imports of TreeModule, but could not be resolved to an NgModule class 8 export declare class MobxAngularModule {`
@shreykene - sorry you are getting an error. Please don't add to closed issues. Can you create a new issue with a way to reproduce the error so that we can investigate please.

Can't UMD have `__export(require('...'))` type re-exports? I thought it could.
You can have commonjs `require` imports but they must be passed to the factory function. I dont see how you could have `require` reexports without breaking non-commonjs formats

My understanding is that you could also have `require(...)` calls inside the factory (what RequireJS calls [simplified CommonJS wrapping][1]). Also, the TypeScript playground seems to generate that format for UMD (but that might be because the playground doesn't do a proper build): [TS playground example][2]

[1]: https://requirejs.org/docs/whyamd.html#sugar 
[2]: https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?target=1&module=3&ssl=1&ssc=1&pln=28&pc=1#code/JYWwDg9gTgLgBAIhgOwM4FoDG0Cm6QQAmArgDY6oD0AhmGKcJtTMBMggNwBQXOAHpFhwAVHABmUCCEQA6SvWZjoILFILtu-QfFESps+aUXLOvAdB3jJ0hHIUwlUFahjNGprRZFX9tw8ad0MEkAN2BCHChUD3MhXWsDKAoIYihMPFIIagioUzNtbz0bOWQ3EIpMKGAwGBkCEnIYgvjfOWwQdTzPOJ9iykliGEimrxa+sWBydFQATxccEBGeooMACxgYMCwGHGQYJcsVv0cQaO58rwBvLjhbuAA1YBwAdwBhI1RUABobu8eX97UT4AWRwrh+dweT2eACVkqRylAIXcAOZg-5vD7fX63NEwDGg8E4uDAVAAaWQEGeyAxyNuSRRpKGUAAouQQLsYD8AL69Aw4dmc9AMplQGZ5bBoeBKCBwAC8cAA2jIVQByACMACYAMyqgC63CAA

OK, so AMD supports a `require` argument passed through to the factory function, so 
I guess it is possible and we should perhaps support it... But in that case you cannot use the UMD templates that support globals. See https://github.com/umdjs/umd

I am not arguing whether it is a good idea or not to use `require()` calls in UMD, but if it is possible that the UMD files we need to process use that, then it would be better if we detected it.

I'd be happy to add support for this in a PR I am working on to fix star re-exports with imported helpers.
For reference: #34512
